common_name: Gillian Daylily (Lavender with Blackcurrant Eye, Parent of Jane Trimmer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Trimmer introduction, registered in 1999, carries evergreen, reblooming foliage.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Gillian bears large, flat-form lavender flowers about four and a half inches across with a bold, sharply defined blackcurrant-purple eye and matching picotee edge. Registered by hybridizer Dan Trimmer in 1999 from a cross of Moonlit Masquerade and Dragon's Eye, this tetraploid blooms in early season on evergreen, reblooming foliage and was later used as a parent of Jane Trimmer. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Sabine Baur Daylily (Ivory with Royal Purple Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid introduction, registered in 1997, carries evergreen foliage and blooms into the evening, reopening the next day.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Sabine Baur bears large, ruffled, creamy ivory flowers with a bold royal-purple eye and matching picotee edge, opening in late afternoon and remaining open into the following day. Registered in 1997, this tetraploid daylily earned the AHS Don C. Stevens Award for best eyed cultivar in 2003 along with an Award of Merit in 2005, and was later used as a parent of Jane Trimmer. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Kings Throne Daylily (Lavender-Orchid Bitone, Parent of Ocean Rain)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this vigorous, well-branched daylily carries semi-evergreen foliage and was used by hybridizer Curt Hanson as a parent of his first registered introduction, Ocean Rain.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Kings Throne bears large, six-inch lavender-orchid bitone flowers with a darker eyezone, carried on vigorous, well-branched scapes about two feet tall. It blooms in mid-season on semi-evergreen foliage and was used by hybridizer Curt Hanson, crossed with Enchanted Empress, to produce his first registered daylily, Ocean Rain, in 1987. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Enchanted Empress Daylily (Fragrant Cream-Pink Crispate Rebloomer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Munson introduction, registered in 1980, carries evergreen foliage and reblooms reliably with its fragrant, ruffle-edged crispate flowers.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Enchanted Empress bears fragrant, six-inch, crispate-form flowers in a soft cream-pink self with a cream throat, carried on scapes about 26 inches tall. Registered by R.W. Munson in 1980, this early-season rebloomer earned the AHS Honorable Mention in 1986, and was crossed with Kings Throne by hybridizer Curt Hanson to produce his first registered daylily, Ocean Rain, in 1987. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Celestial Virgins Daylily (Strawberry-Pink Blend, Parent of Electric Ladyland)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Hanson introduction, registered in 2009 from Ruffled Strawberry Parfait crossed with a seedling, carries semi-evergreen foliage.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Celestial Virgins bears five-inch, strawberry-pink blend flowers above a chartreuse throat, carried on well-branched, 36-inch scapes. This tetraploid Hanson introduction, registered in 2009 from a cross of Ruffled Strawberry Parfait and a seedling, blooms midseason into late season on semi-evergreen foliage and was later used, crossed with Prometheus Revisited, as a parent of Electric Ladyland. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring, spacing to allow good airflow; this historic East Malling floricane type was a widely grown early-season English raspberry through the mid-20th century.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Malling Promise is a vigorous early-season floricane raspberry raised at England's East Malling Research Station and introduced in 1946, bearing medium-sized, conical, bright red berries with a well-balanced sweet-tart flavor from late June into July. It is fully hardy and tolerates a range of soils, and its vigorous habit contributed to the parentage of later Malling-series cultivars. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and thin new canes to the strongest few per foot of row.
sources: East Malling Research Station historical variety records
